newsitem.title: USA: Police flooded with calls on Cosby murder suspect.
newsitem.headline: Police flooded with calls on Cosby murder suspect.

text.p: Police investigating the murder of entertainer Bill Cosby's son were flooded with calls on Sunday from people who claimed to know something about the suspected killer shown in a newly released composite sketch.

Detectives were working around the clock to follow up on the new leads, which started pouring in after a drawing of a white man with a menacing stare appeared on local news broadcasts on Saturday night.
"There have been numerous calls, and they are all being referred to Robbery Homicide," said Officer Vincent Aguirre, a Los Angeles police spokesman, referring to the elite squad handling the case.

While admitting that investigators looking into Ennis Cosby's murder have "no real suspect at this point," Aguirre said detectives hope the sketch of the killer -- along with a drawing of a second possible witness -- will lead to a breakthrough.

But first, Aguirre said, police must pick their way through a maze of phone tips, including those from people who insist they have had dreams that could help investigators solve the murder. "Obviously we won't be following up on some of these calls," he said.

Ennis Cosby, a 27-year-old Columbia University graduate student who was finishing a two-week vacation in Los Angeles, was killed by an unidentified gunman early on Thursday morning while changing a flat tire on a darkened roadside.

At his family's request, his body was released on Saturday from the county morgue following an autopsy that confirmed he died from a single bullet to the head, officials said. Arrangements for a private funeral were pending.
The famed comedian, his wife Camille and their four daughters remained in seclusion at a secret location somewhere in the East.

A grieving Cosby told publicist and longtime friend David Brokaw that he was struggling hard to cope with the loss of his only son, who was the inspiration for some of his most touching television comedy.
"Your concentration goes in 18 different directions," Cosby was quoted as saying. "You try to pull things back together but it's like playing with oil and water."
Enlisting the public's help in solving a murder that has shocked the nation, police released a drawing based on the description provided by a woman who saw part of the attack.

The witness, a 47-year-old screenwriter, was said to be a friend who came to help Cosby change a flat tire. When a man with a pistol accosted them, she fled the scene in fear, only to return and find Cosby lying dead next to his Mercedes convertible, a source close to the investigation said.
Police said it took until Saturday to complete the sketch because the woman had been so traumatized by the slaying and by the crush of news media attention.

The killer was described as being of average height and weight, between the ages of 25 and 32 and wearing a light-coloured knit cap. Investigators said he was on foot and that robbery was his likely motive.

Police also released a drawing of a possible witness -- a white man in his late 20s or early 30s with a moustache and goatee wearing a dark beret. He may have been driving past at the time of the roadside killing but has yet to come forward.
After talking to Cosby late on Saturday, his publicist said he seemed "very composed and focused, but it's hard for any of us to imagine what he's dealing with inside."

Even while grieving in private, Cosby has taken time to comfort the mother of a 17-year-old girl who was killed by an armed gang member while riding a city bus in Los Angeles only hours after his son's murder.

In a message left on his publicist's answering machine, Cosby challenged tabloid publications and TV shows to offer a reward for information on the killer instead of using their money to buy exclusives.

"It's the tabloids," Cosby said. "They pay money to have witnesses talk and it disrupts the case. Why can't the tabloids put out the word ... that they would pay to have someone come forward, and they could have exclusivity of the story."
